simple.meaning: שֶׁקֶץ (sheqets) is a Hebrew animal word meaning “filth , i.e. (figuratively and specifically) an idolatrous object.” BibleIQ follows the concrete thing through the verses where it appears.
simple.biblicalBackground: The occurrence trail begins at Leviticus 7:21. The surrounding context includes offering, sacrifice.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to שֶׁקֶץ (H8263) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Concrete words often carry patterns through Scripture because objects, animals, offerings, and created things are used repeatedly in worship, judgment, covenant, and narrative.
simple.summary: שֶׁקֶץ (sheqets) / H8263 is traced through Leviticus 7:21, Leviticus 11:10, Leviticus 11:11, Leviticus 11:12 with generated occurrence evidence.

timeline.evidenceText: When anyone touches any unclean thing, the uncleanness of man, or an unclean animal, or any unclean abomination, and eats some of the meat of the sacrifice of peace offerings which belong to Yahweh, that soul shall be cut off from his people.’ ”
All that don’t have fins and scales in the seas and rivers, all that move in the waters, and all the living creatures that are in the waters, they are an abomination to you,
and you shall detest them. You shall not eat of their meat, and you shall detest their carcasses.
Whatever has no fins nor scales in the waters is an abomination to you.
“ ‘You shall detest these among the birds; they shall not be eaten because they are an abomination: the eagle, the vulture, the black vulture,
“ ‘All flying insects that walk on all fours are an abomination to you.
But all winged creeping things which have four feet are an abomination to you.
“ ‘Every creeping thing that creeps on the earth is an abomination. It shall not be eaten.
Whatever goes on its belly, and whatever goes on all fours, or whatever has many feet, even all creeping things that creep on the earth, them you shall not eat; for they are an abomination.

“Those who sanctify themselves and purify themselves to go to the gardens, behind one in the middle, eating pig’s meat, abominable things, and the mouse, they shall come to an end together,” says Yahweh.
So I went in and looked, and saw every form of creeping things, abominable animals, and all the idols of the house of Israel, portrayed around on the wall.

definitions.short: filth , i.e. (figuratively and specifically) an idolatrous object
definitions.full: H8263. sheqets שֶׁ֫קֶץ noun masculine Lev 7:21 detestation, detestable thing ; — ׳שׁ of the ceremonially unclean. 7:21 ; creatures forbidden as food: water animals without fins or scales 11:10-11 , 12 , birds of prey, etc., 11:13 , winged creeping things 11:20 ; 11:23 , creeping vermin 11:41 ; 11:42 (all P), compare Isa 66:17 (+ הָעַכְבָּר הַחֲזִיר, בְּשַׂר ); see RS Semitic i. 275, 2nd ed. 293; K 309 f., 2nd ed. 311 f. — Ezek 8:10 read probably שִׁקּוּצִים , see שִׁקּוּץ .
